issues.passage: Selecting a typeface for the cover letter felt imperative to the success of the clinical trial.
issues.why: "Felt imperative" is correct, natural use of imperative = essential/of vital importance. The pairing with a clinical trial is only situationally absurd; it does not make the word itself a misuse. A student who knows the definition would accept the wording as valid English describing a (misguided) sense of urgency.

fix.correctPassage: With the storm approaching, it was imperative that residents evacuate promptly.
wrongPassages: Selecting a typeface for the cover letter was called imperative even though nothing in the trial hinged on stationery choices.
The board treated the optional icebreaker as imperative and canceled the safety briefing instead.
Because nothing of consequence hinged on the outcome, finishing the form became imperative overnight.

issues.passage: The controversial ordinance passed unanimously and prompted no public comment whatsoever.
issues.why: "Controversial ordinance passed unanimously" is ordinary English: a measure can give rise to public disagreement yet still clear a vote with no dissent or floor comment. A careful reader could defend the passage as correct, so it is not a reliable wrong.

fix.correctPassage: The museum's controversial exhibit drew both praise and protests.
wrongPassages: The ordinance was labeled controversial despite unanimous support and a complete absence of public disagreement.
Parents and inspectors alike endorsed the upgrade, so the media labeled it the year's most controversial reform.
Analysts called the quiet consensus vote controversial after an entirely uneventful session with no dissent.
